learning_objectives: Identify natural numbers and whole numbers.
Distinguish between natural numbers, whole numbers and integers.

discover.title: Numbers Around Us
discover.prompt: Look around your home, school or community. Where do you encounter numbers?
activities: Observe numbers on a classroom door or house.
Identify numbers used when counting books, people or money.
discover.reflection_question: Why would everyday life become difficult without numbers?

learn.title: Understanding Numbers
learn.explanation: Numbers are mathematical symbols used to count, measure, compare and describe quantities.

concepts.name: Integers
concepts.definition: Positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers and zero.

worked_examples.question: Is 7 a natural number?
worked_examples.solution: Yes. Seven is a counting number.

worked_examples.question: Is 0 a whole number?
worked_examples.solution: Yes. Zero belongs to the set of whole numbers.

worked_examples.question: Is -4 an integer?
worked_examples.solution: Yes. Negative whole numbers are integers.

learn.key_point: Every natural number is a whole number, and every whole number is an integer. Zero is not included in the natural numbers under the convention used in this lesson.

practice.instructions: Classify each number according to the number system.

questions.question: Classify the number 5.
questions.expected_answer: Natural number, whole number and integer.

questions.question: Write three examples of natural numbers.

knowledge_check.instructions: Answer the following questions without looking at the lesson notes.

questions.question: Which of the following is a whole number?
Which number is an integer but not a whole number?
What is the difference between natural numbers and whole numbers?
questions.expected_answer: Whole numbers include zero, while natural numbers in this lesson begin at one.

apply.title: Mathematics in Daily Life
apply.scenario: A learner records the temperature of a town as -2 degrees Celsius in the morning and 5 degrees Celsius in the afternoon.
tasks: Explain why negative numbers are useful when recording temperature.

voice.prompt: Explain the difference between natural numbers, whole numbers and integers in your own words.

prompts: What new mathematical idea did I learn today?
Where can I use this knowledge in everyday life?
What do I need to practise further?

questions.question: Give four examples of whole numbers.
Give one practical use of negative numbers.

mastery_criteria: Correctly identifies natural numbers, whole numbers and integers.
Explains the differences between the three number systems.
Applies number concepts to a practical situation.
evidence_and_mastery.remediation: Learners scoring below the mastery threshold should revisit the explanation, study additional examples and complete guided practice before attempting reassessment.
